title: local-auth-429-401-scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad while debugging recurring 401 and 429 reports from mobile clients (iOS SDK + backend proxy). Keep notes of commands tried, log extracts, hypotheses, and short-term mitigations. Not polished — for context when I hand off to SE or SRE.

Observed symptoms (summary):
- Mobile app intermittently gets 401 Unauthorized responses while using stored API key -> happens more after midnight UTC.
- Separate bursts of 429 Too Many Requests for same service account key (backend batch job).
- Users and internal client both see 401s; sometimes 401s followed immediately by 429s in same session.

Quick timeline of recent incidents:
- 2026-03-02 03:12 UTC: first user report (iOS) — 401 on chat completion endpoint.
- 2026-03-02 03:15 UTC: internal worker spike (cron job) ran retry storm, received 429s.
- 2026-03-04 22:00 UTC: rotated key for service-account-analytics as temporary mitigation. 401s persisted for some mobile clients.
- 2026-03-07 11:47 UTC: reproduced locally; saw 401 when client clock intentionally skewed by +5 minutes.

Repro steps I used locally (keep commands):
1) basic curl with stored API key (failed with 401):
   curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n     -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX' \n     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n     -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'

   Response snippet: (headers + body)
   HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
   Date: Wed, 02 Mar 2026 03:12:09 GMT
   Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
   content-length: 73

   {"error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"API key invalid or expired"}}

2) same call using admin rotated key (succeeds) -> confirms key-specific issue.
   curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_test_ROTATED' ...
   HTTP/1.1 200 OK

3) hit quota introspect endpoint (internal):
   curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-token' https://internal.redwood/v1/keys/introspect?key=sk_live_XXXX
   -> output: key_id, created_at, last_used_at, quota_limit_per_minute, status=active
   Note: last_used_at shows bursts at 03:15 UTC from host=analytics-worker-3

4) reproduce 429 pattern: run 200 parallel requests using hey/http_load against same key -> got 429 once pool exhausted:
   hey -n 200 -c 50 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_CONCURRENT" -d '{...}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

   Observed headers on 429 response:
   HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
   x-ratelimit-limit: 60
   x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
   x-ratelimit-reset: 167//(unix)
   retry-after: 10
   {"error":{"type":"rate_limit_error","message":"rate limit exceeded"}}

Commands / probes tried to triage cause:
- Verified clock skew hypothesis: skewed local clock by +5m and replayed request -> JWT-based keys rejected with exp error in auth service logs. (So clock skew is a real possibility for JWTs or signed timestamps.)
- Checked KMS/rotation: rotated sk_test key and invalidated caches; some mobile clients still hit 401 -> likely cached credential in app or proxy layer.
- Introspected key usage via metrics: queried kafka event stream for "auth_fail" events: found pattern user-agent: okhttp/4.9.3 had higher 401s.
- Tested removing proxy layer: direct call from mobile-device emulator -> 401 persists for subset of installs (same app version).
- Confirmed that 429 bursts correlate with batch jobs that do naive retries without exponential backoff.

Partial log extracts (sanitized):
- 2026-03-02T03:12:09Z request_id=abc123 client_ip=52.45.12.33 method=POST path=/v1/chat status=401 auth_key=sk_live_XXXX auth_reason=expired_token
- 2026-03-02T03:15:02Z request_id=def456 client_ip=10.9.81.33 method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=429 ratelimit_key=service:analytics worker_id=analytics-worker-3
- 2026-03-07T11:47:12Z request_id=ghi789 method=POST auth_reason=timestamp_skew skew_seconds=323

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Client clock skew + signed timestamp/JWT expiry -> intermittent 401s for mobile devices whose system clocks drift. Evidence: reproduces when skewed, logs show skew_seconds. Likelihood: high for subset of users.
2) Stale cached API keys in our CDN/edge/proxy layer: we rotated key but CDN cached old key validation result causing 401 until cache TTL expired. Likelihood: medium.
3) Global quota/route-level throttling misapplied to certain keys -> returns 429 for background batch jobs and then 401 for follow-up calls due to temporary block state in gateway. Likelihood: medium-low.
4) Credentials compromised and then revoked -> would see revocation in internal audit. No evidence yet. Likelihood: low.

Things to check next (actionable):
- Add a query to log pipeline to measure "skew_seconds" distribution across 30 days for affected UA strings. (Linear: PROD-512)
- Check CDN/edge cache rules for auth verification endpoint responses. Ensure cache-control: private on auth introspect responses.
- Patch mobile SDK to detect large clock skew and warn user (or fallback to server time via /time endpoint).
- Add per-job backoff + jitter in analytics cron to reduce 429 storms.
- Short-term: rotate the key (done), but also revoke any sessions associated with the old key. Ensure clients fetch new key at next login.

Mitigations applied & results: 
- 2026-03-04 rotated analytics key -> reduced 401s for server-side processes, mobile clients unaffected.
- 2026-03-07 deployed short probe that rejects requests with timestamp_skew>300s earlier in the auth layer and returns friendly message with suggestion to sync clock -> recorded fewer 401 confused tickets.

Notes on headers to monitor (server-side):
- x-ratelimit-limit
- x-ratelimit-remaining
- x-ratelimit-reset (unix epoch)
- retry-after (seconds)
- x-auth-expiry (custom header we may add indicating token TTL)

Ideas for longer-term fixes:
- Switch mobile API keys to short-lived session tokens derived from refresh tokens; server enforces device clock check on handshake and returns server-time.
- Improve client SDK to do aggressive jittered backoff for 429 and avoid synchronous fan-out on boot.
- Harden gateway: ensure per-key counters are correct and consistent across regions (global rate limit coordination bug suspicion). Add a debug endpoint to inspect in-memory counters by key.

Outstanding questions to triage with SRE/infra:
- Do we have any global WAF rules that could convert auth failures to 401s? (I asked infra)
- Are there any proxy retries that strip Authorization header on retries? If so, that would explain 401 happening only after a gateway retry.
- Confirm whether rotated keys were fully propagated to edge caches (TTL) at time of rotation.

Quick copy-paste checklist for reproducing next time:
1) Confirm client time: date -u; if off, record skew in seconds.
2) Reproduce with direct curl using exact Authorization header (no proxy).
3) Query introspect endpoint: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin' https://internal/keys/introspect?key=<dirty-key>
4) Tail logs for request_id returned in client error: kibana query: request_id:<id> AND path:/v1/chat*
5) If 429, save full headers and body, pay attention to retry-after and x-ratelimit-remaining.

Random notes / heuristics I wrote down while debugging:
- Mobile SDK historically had bug where device time resets to 1970 on low-battery event -> real world device clock skew = known recurring cause.
- When we see 401 spikes clustered by UA string + os_version, prioritize shipping SDK update to that cohort.
- For 429: if x-ratelimit-remaining==0 but other keys still have allowance, likely per-key limit correct. If multiple keys all show low remaining simultaneously, look for global bucket exhaustion.

Hand-off to SE: attach this doc, include repro steps and test keys used, and link to Linear PROD-512. If I can't close this by EOD, need SRE to enable debug-logs for auth service for keys: sk_live_* for next 24h.

End of scratchpad.
